findings.where: First screen, the header lockup: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Mark's name is set small and in a regular weight, about the size of the nav links. The arches of the mark beside it are far bigger and heavier. A first look lands on the firm's logo, and the name reads like a caption to it rather than the thing that leads.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark. The brief's personal-advisor test asks that his name lead with the logo beside it, and a visitor from a development bank sees the firm's mark first and the person second.

findings.where: Article specimen, the title block: 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' and the byline 'Mark M. Moseley · Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The byline sits almost against the title's descenders, much closer than any other gap on a page that claims an even 32 px rhythm. It reads as crammed under the title, not set as a separate line, and the rhythm the specimen promises is broken at its first step.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles, who sees a tight, unfinished head on the page. The founder too, who asked for a rhythm that holds without hand-tuned offsets.

findings.where: Article specimen, the PDF list entry: 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge' and 'Lecture · 23 April 2026' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The entry's title and meta line start a few pixels to the right of the column's left edge, which the body text, subhead, list and rule above all share. The slip is small enough to look like a mistake, not a choice.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader, or Mark, looking down the left edge of a page meant to feel like a well-set legal journal. A ragged start there undercuts the refined impression.
